title: Pneumonia in a patient with COPD
summary: Pneumonia in someone with COPD calls for the COPD-with-lower-respiratory-infection code on top of the pneumonia code; it is not a COPD flare.

documents.author: H. Iverson, MD (Radiology)
documents.text:
EXAM: XR chest PA and lateral.
FINDINGS: Dense consolidation left lower lobe with air bronchograms. Hyperinflated lungs with flattened hemidiaphragms, consistent with emphysematous change. No effusion. Normal heart size.
IMPRESSION: 1. Left lower lobe pneumonia. 2. Chronic emphysematous changes.

documents.author: E. Moreau, MD (Emergency Medicine)
documents.text:
CC: cough, fever, SOB.
HPI: 69 y/o M with COPD (no home O2), HTN, HLD, GERD, current smoker 1 ppd, presents with 3 days productive cough with green sputum, fevers to 38.6, pleuritic L-sided chest pain, and increased SOB. Using albuterol 2-3x/day (usual 1x/day). No sick contacts.
Vitals: T 38.4, HR 104, RR 22, BP 142/84, SpO2 90% RA -> 94% on 2 L NC.
Exam: Mild increased WOB, speaking full sentences. Bronchial breath sounds and crackles L base. Scattered end-expiratory wheeze (pt states "always a little wheezy"). No edema.
Labs: WBC 15.4 (88% PMN). Na 136, K 4.2, Cr 1.0, BUN 17. Procalcitonin 1.8. Lactate 1.6. VBG pH 7.39 / pCO2 46.
CXR: LLL consolidation.
ED course: Duoneb x1, ceftriaxone 1 g + azithromycin 500 mg IV. R/o COPD exacerbation.
Impression: LLL pneumonia in COPD patient. Admit to hospitalist.

documents.author: F. Beaumont, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
HISTORY AND PHYSICAL
HPI: 69M, COPD GOLD 3 (FEV1 44% predicted, 2025), active smoker 45 pack-years, presents with 3 days productive cough, fever, pleuritic pain, LLL consolidation on CXR, WBC 15.4, PCT 1.8.
PMH: COPD on tiotropium/olodaterol, HTN, HLD, GERD. Meds: tiotropium/olodaterol 2 puffs daily, albuterol PRN, amlodipine 5 mg, simvastatin 20 mg, pantoprazole 40 mg.
SH: smokes 1 ppd, interested in quitting. No EtOH.
Exam: T 38.1, HR 98, RR 20, SpO2 93% 2 L. LLL crackles, bronchial BS. Mild baseline expiratory wheeze, good air movement, no accessory muscle use.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. Community-acquired pneumonia, LLL, bacterial - ceftriaxone 1 g daily + azithromycin x 3 days. Sputum cx, strep/legionella urine Ag. O2 to SpO2 88-92%.
2. COPD with acute lower respiratory infection (the LLL pneumonia). I do not think this is a COPD exacerbation: wheeze at baseline per pt, good air movement, VBG with normal pH. Continue home tiotropium/olodaterol, albuterol PRN. No systemic steroids.
3. Tobacco use disorder, cigarettes - nicotine patch 21 mg, cessation counseling.
4. HTN - continue amlodipine.
5. HLD - continue simvastatin.
6. GERD - continue pantoprazole.
DVT ppx enoxaparin. Full code.

documents.author: F. Beaumont, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
S: Less SOB, pleuritic pain improved, cough productive. Slept OK.
O: Tmax 37.6, HR 86, RR 18, SpO2 92% on 1 L, 90% RA at rest. Lungs: LLL crackles, minimal wheeze. WBC 11.0. Strep pneumo and legionella urine Ag negative. Sputum cx: normal respiratory flora.
A/P:
1. LLL community-acquired pneumonia, organism not identified - continue ceftriaxone, d/c azithro after dose 3. Wean O2.
2. COPD with acute lower respiratory infection - stable, no exacerbation, no steroids needed.
3. Tobacco use disorder - patch, counseling done.
4. HTN, HLD, GERD - home meds.

documents.author: J. Park, RN
documents.text: Pt resting, no acute distress. Weaned to RA at 22:00 per protocol, SpO2 90-92% at rest, 89-90% ambulating to BR, recovered quickly with pursed-lip breathing. Productive cough, small amt yellow sputum. Lungs diminished L base. Using home inhaler as scheduled, albuterol x1 overnight. Nicotine patch in place, pt asked for cessation pamphlet, provided. Afebrile. Voiding qs. Ambulating independently.

documents.author: F. Beaumont, MD (Hospital Medicine)
documents.text:
DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 09/15/2026 - Discharge 09/18/2026. Home.
Principal diagnosis: Community-acquired pneumonia, left lower lobe.
Secondary diagnoses: COPD with acute lower respiratory infection (no exacerbation). Nicotine dependence, cigarettes. Hypertension. Hyperlipidemia. GERD.
Hospital course: Treated with ceftriaxone/azithromycin with clinical improvement; weaned to room air HD3 (SpO2 92% RA at rest and 90% with ambulation, no home O2 needed). Urine antigens negative and sputum culture with normal flora; no organism identified. COPD remained at baseline throughout without steroids.
Discharge meds: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875 mg BID x 3 days; home inhalers; nicotine patch 21 mg daily; amlodipine, simvastatin, pantoprazole.
Follow-up: PCP 1 week; pulmonary clinic 6 weeks; repeat CXR 6-8 weeks; smoking cessation program referral placed.

gold.explanation: Pneumonia in a COPD patient is coded with the infection (J18.9, no organism identified) plus J44.0, COPD with acute lower respiratory infection. J44.0 is a CC, giving DRG 194. The attending states explicitly and repeatedly that this is not a COPD exacerbation, so J44.1 doesn't apply, and plain J44.9 misses the combination code. A naive system codes J44.9 or follows the ED's 'r/o COPD exacerbation' to J44.1.
